provider: JFrog Artifactory Cloud — free tier (historically 2 GB)

free_tier.stated: 2 GB total storage + 10 GB/month data transfer on the legacy 'JFrog Free' cloud subscription. That tier is no longer generally available: JFrog's own blog now carries the banner 'The below post showcases the JFrog Platform Free Tier, which is currently limited for new sign-ups.' The live pricing page has no free tier at all. The entry point is Pro at $50/mo with 25 GB base consumption.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: 2 GB total storage (not per month. A Stack Overflow answer from a JFrog employee confirms it is total, and you must delete to reclaim); 10 GB/month transfer; 2,000 build minutes; 21-day inactivity deactivation.

egress.terms: 10 GB/month included on the legacy free tier; beyond that the platform bills 'Consumption = Storage + Transfer' against the included base. Not free, not Cloudflare-coverable.

interface_detail: rest (Artifactory REST), JFrog CLI, native package clients, OCI
tooling: JFrog CLI, `curl -T`, `docker push`, `twine upload`. Best-in-class tooling, which is why the 2 GB cap is such a shame.
chaining: Previously: one free cloud instance per account, × unlimited accounts, at 2 GB each. Now gated: 'limited for new sign-ups', and accounts are deactivated after '21 days with no data transfer activity'. So a dormant bulk store dies.
limits_note: 2 GB total storage (not per month. A Stack Overflow answer from a JFrog employee confirms it is total, and you must delete to reclaim); 10 GB/month transfer; 2,000 build minutes; 21-day inactivity deactivation.
